newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs surge as rate fears subside.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs surge as rate fears subside.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rose sharply in active trade on Wednesday as expectations of a Japanese rate hike dwindled in the face of the yen's gathering strength.
"A couple of weeks back, sentiment was quite strong that they would raise rates. Now the expectation seems to be 50:50," a trader with a European futures house said.
The dollar fell to its lowest levels in almost seven months against the yen on concerns a growing Japanese current account surplus would fuel trade tensions between the U.S. and Japan.
Recent signs of continued weakness in Japan's economic recovery have dampened market fears a rate hike was on the cards by year end.
Dealers said the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s generous money market operations also boosted sentiment in the interest rate futures market.

"The BOJ really surprised the market by injecting 300 billion yen into the market against expectations that they would inject 100 billion or not do anything," a trader at a European futures house said.
He said locals were good buyers of Euroyen futures on SIMEX.
The lead December Euroyen stood at their day high of 99.07 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 98.95 on hefty volume of 35,895 lots.
September JGBs ended at 123.87 against their previous 123.23. Near-term resistance is seen at 124.00.
Dealers said the market was likely to turn cautious nearer the release of the BOJ's quarterly business sentiment survey on June 25.
"I think there'll be some long liquidations towards the tankan. I would want to be a seller then," the trader said.
Eurodollar futures ended firmer with the December contract at 93.825 against its IMM close at 93.810.
